title: Visit a masjid for the first time
whyMatters: A masjid gives you somewhere to pray, people to ask, classes, and company. Your first visit does not have to go perfectly. It only has to be small enough that you actually go.

subSteps: An ordinary daily prayer is much easier than a packed Friday.
Check the masjid website or phone ahead if you are unsure.
Ask whether they have anything for new Muslims or for visitors.
Wear clean, loose clothing that covers you comfortably.
Women can bring a scarf if they plan to enter the prayer area.
Do not panic if you are not dressed like everyone else.
Take your shoes off where you see others taking theirs off.
If you are not sure where to go, ask someone near the entrance.
Saying you are a new Muslim and this is your first time here is enough.
Ask who handles convert support or beginner classes.
If it becomes too much, leave. You can come back another day.

obstacles.problem: I am afraid people will stare
obstacles.solution: Most people are focused on their own prayer. If someone does notice you are new, they will usually want to help. You can also phone ahead and ask whether someone can meet you at the door.

obstacles.problem: I do not know which entrance to use
obstacles.solution: Look for signs, follow where people are heading, or ask at the door. Some masjids have separate prayer areas, and asking about it is completely normal.

tinyVersion: Phone or message one masjid and ask when a beginner can come by.
unlocksNext: Once you have been through the door once, Jumuah, classes, and finding a mentor all get easier.

commonQuestions.problem: Can I visit if I cannot pray properly yet?
commonQuestions.solution: Yes. You can watch, follow what you can, and ask for help. A masjid is meant to be a place to learn, not a room reserved for people who already know everything.

gentleScripts.title: At the entrance
gentleScripts.body: Assalamu alaykum. I am a new Muslim and this is my first time here. Could you show me where to go?
